name: Preference-Based Teaching Dimension
definition: The **Preference-Based Teaching Dimension** is the minimum, over strict preference orders on $\mathcal{H}$, of the largest number of labeled examples needed to make the target the uniquely most preferred concept consistent with its teaching sample.
graph_summary: Smallest worst-case teaching-sample size after optimizing a fixed preference order.

monotonic.proof: Restrict any strict preference order and its teaching samples to a subfamily. Each sample still makes its target uniquely most preferred among the fewer consistent candidates, so the optimum cannot increase.

c_monotonic.proof: Restrict the preference order and the teaching map to the conditioned fibre, deleting fixed coordinates from samples; the teaching guarantee is preserved.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

p_monotonic.proof: This parameter is exactly equal to Recursive Teaching Dimension by the established relationship `preferencebased_teaching_dimension_recursive_teaching_dimension`; its p monotonic classification transfers unchanged.
